$comment: BeBold refusal policy, version 1. THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH.
It is pure data so that someone who reads a writing system better than they read
JavaScript can change a verdict and open a pull request without touching code.
policy.js is GENERATED from this file by tools/build-policy.mjs and CI fails if the
two drift. After editing, run: npm run build:policy
Patterns are {pattern, flags} pairs compiled with new RegExp(pattern, flags).

elements.$comment: Tag names whose text is never treated, grouped by the reason why.

nonText.why: Not prose, or not rendered as text at all.

controls.why: Interactive control labels are UI affordances, not reading material. Bolding them adds visual noise with no reading benefit.

codeish.why: Character-level accuracy beats reading speed. A misread character in code is a bug.

$comment: Families declined by default, each with a per-family opt-in in the options page.
Declining is a stated policy, not a gap: Intl.Segmenter segments all of these
correctly. The question is whether 'the first half of a word' is a coherent
visual unit, and in these systems it is not.
Scripts NOT listed here are treated: Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Hebrew and others.
Hebrew is treated because its square-script letters do not connect, so a prefix

arabic.why: Letters take positional forms and join, so emphasising a prefix cuts across a connected ligature.

brahmic.why: Vowel signs reorder visually, so the first n letters are not the leftmost n glyphs.

cjk.why: Words are often one or two characters, so half a word is half a sentence rather than an anchor.

seasia.why: Word boundaries are detected correctly, but the visual result has not been validated by a native reader.

$comment: Runs of raw text that must never be split, matched against the WHOLE text node
rather than per word. Intl.Segmenter would otherwise hand us 'https', 'example'

iconFonts.why: Ligature icon fonts render words like 'menu' as a single glyph. Splitting one is nonsense.

credentialFields.$comment: A VISIBLE match refuses the whole document. A hidden one only excludes its own form subtree, because a collapsed login form in a site's chrome is not a banking page.
credentialFields.selector: input[type="password"],[autocomplete*="cc-number" i],[autocomplete*="cc-exp" i],[autocomplete*="cc-csc" i],[autocomplete*="cc-name" i],[autocomplete*="one-time-code" i],[autocomplete*="current-password" i],[autocomplete*="new-password" i]

siteOptOut.$comment: Any site can decline declaratively, no negotiation required.
